title: Double Taxation Relief for NRBs in UK USA & Canada
metaDescription: Avoid paying tax twice on Dhaka rental, bank interest, and property sale income using Bangladesh DTAA treaties and Income Tax Act 2023 credit rules.
heroIntro: Non-Resident Bangladeshis (NRBs) in the UK, USA, and Canada can avoid paying income tax twice on Dhaka rental income, bank interest, or capital gains by claiming relief under Bangladesh's Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAAs) and Sections 244–245 of the Income Tax Act, 2023. Proper tax residency certificates and NBR return filings unlock foreign tax credits in both jurisdictions.

quickAnswer.heading: At a Glance: NRB Double Taxation Relief
points: Primary Statute: Income Tax Act, 2023 (Sections 244 & 245) & Bilateral DTAAs (UK, USA, Canada).

Core Relief Mechanism: Foreign Tax Credit (offsetting tax paid in Bangladesh against home-country tax).
Key Document: Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) + NBR Acknowledgement Slip & Tax Payment Challan.

sections.h2: How Double Taxation Affects NRBs with Bangladesh Income
sections.content:
Global income taxation in the UK, USA, and Canada requires tax residents to report worldwide income—including Dhaka apartment rent, fixed-deposit interest, and property sale capital gains—even when tax has already been deducted at source in Bangladesh. Without invoking a bilateral tax treaty, an NRB could pay 15%–30% withholding or capital gains tax in Bangladesh and then pay full domestic income tax abroad on the same earnings.

Under Section 2(45) of the Income Tax Act, 2023, an individual is a non-resident for tax purposes if they stay in Bangladesh for fewer than 183 days in an income year (July–June). Non-residents are taxed in Bangladesh only on income accruing or arising in Bangladesh, while remittance sent through official banking channels remains tax-exempt.

NRBs planning to repatriate property sale proceeds should also review our guide on NBR remittance rules for NRBs and legal money transfer tax rules.

Sections 244 and 245 of the Income Tax Act, 2023 empower the National Board of Revenue (NBR) to enforce bilateral Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements and grant tax credits where income is taxed in two jurisdictions. Where a treaty provision conflicts with domestic tax rates, the treaty rate or relief rule prevails to the extent beneficial to the taxpayer.

For example, if an NRB earns rental income from a house in Uttara or Gulshan, income tax is assessed in Bangladesh under the 'Income from House Property' head after allowable statutory deductions. By filing an annual NBR return and obtaining an official Tax Payment Challan (A-Challan), the NRB can present proof of Bangladeshi tax paid to HMRC (UK), the IRS (USA), or the CRA (Canada) to claim a Foreign Tax Credit.

If you receive a mismatch or audit notice from NBR, consult an experienced tax lawyer in Bangladesh before submitting responses.

sections.h2: Treaty Rules: Bangladesh–UK, USA & Canada DTAAs
sections.content:
Bangladesh maintains active Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements with the United Kingdom (1979), the United States (2004), and Canada (1982), allocating primary taxing rights by income type.

Income TypePrimary Taxing CountryTreaty Relief Mechanism
Dhaka Rental / Immovable PropertyBangladesh (Situs of Property)Report abroad and claim Foreign Tax Credit for NBR tax paid.
Property Sale Capital GainsBangladeshOffset source-deducted gain tax against UK/US/Canada capital gains tax.
Bangladesh Bank Interest / DividendsShared (Capped Withholding)Treaty caps source withholding (typically 10%–15%) with TRC submission.
Foreign Salary Remitted to BDHost Country (UK/USA/Canada)Foreign-earned salary remitted via legal banking channels is exempt in BD.

When selling ancestral land, NRBs should also verify e-Mutation compliance and Power of Attorney rules so capital gains tax challans are issued in the owner's correct TIN.

sections.h2: Step-by-Step Process to Claim DTAA Relief
sections.content:
Claiming double taxation relief requires coordinated filings in both Bangladesh and your country of residence before respective statutory deadlines.

  1. Verify Non-Resident TIN & Circle: Ensure your 12-digit e-TIN profile with NBR reflects your non-resident status and overseas address.
  2. Obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC): Request a TRC from HMRC, IRS (Form 6166), or CRA confirming you are a tax resident of that treaty country for the relevant tax year.
  3. File Annual NBR Income Tax Return: Submit your Bangladeshi return declaring Dhaka rent, FDR interest, or capital gains and pay net tax via A-Challan—see our Bangladesh tax return filing guide.
  4. Collect Certified Tax Paid Proof: Download your NBR Return Acknowledgement Slip, Assessment Order (if applicable), and verified A-Challan copies.
  5. Claim Foreign Tax Credit Abroad: Attach the NBR tax proof to your UK Self Assessment, US Form 1116, or Canadian T2209 schedule, or engage Advocate Md. Shah Alam for NBR representation and tax certificate coordination.

sections.h2: Documents Checklist for NRB Tax Credit Filing
sections.content:
Maintain a clean audit trail of both Bangladeshi and overseas tax records to prevent remittance holds or double-tax assessments.

  • 12-digit Bangladesh e-TIN certificate and passport travel-history pages proving <183 days stay in Bangladesh.
  • Official Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by HMRC, IRS, or CRA.
  • Annual NBR Income Tax Return copy, Acknowledgement Slip, and verified A-Challan / withholding tax (TDS) certificates from banks.
  • Registered lease agreements, khatian records, or Saf Kabala sale deeds for rental/capital gain verification.
  • Bank inward remittance certificates (Form C / Encashment Certificate) for funds transferred to or from Bangladesh.

NRB business owners should also review non-resident company registration in Bangladesh or visit our NRB Legal Help Desk. You can book a free initial consultation to review your tax notices or property sale tax plan.

faqs.question: Do NRBs have to file an income tax return in Bangladesh if they have no local income?
faqs.answer: If an NRB has no taxable income in Bangladesh and does not hold assets requiring mandatory return filing (such as a registered motor vehicle or active trade licence), a return may not be triggered. However, if you own Dhaka property or sell land, filing an NBR return is essential.

faqs.question: Is money sent by an NRB to family in Bangladesh taxable under the Income Tax Act, 2023?
faqs.answer: No. Remittance sent by a Non-Resident Bangladeshi from abroad through official banking channels is exempt from income tax in Bangladesh. Keep bank encashment certificates or remittance slips so NBR can verify the foreign source if questioned during asset scrutiny.

faqs.question: Can an NRB claim a refund if Bangladeshi banks deducted 15% instead of 10% treaty rate?
faqs.answer: Yes, in principle, if you submit a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) under the applicable DTAA, the lower treaty withholding rate applies on interest or dividends. Excess tax deducted at source can be adjusted or claimed when filing your annual NBR tax return.

faqs.question: What happens if an NRB stays in Bangladesh for 183 days or more in a year?
faqs.answer: Under Section 2(45) of the Income Tax Act, 2023, staying 183 days or more in an income year (or 90 days if present 365+ days in the prior 4 years) makes you a tax resident in Bangladesh. Residents are subject to broader worldwide income reporting unless treaty tie-breaker rules apply.

faqs.question: Can a lawyer file my NBR income tax return and handle notices while I am abroad?
faqs.answer: Yes. By executing a Power of Attorney or tax authorisation letter, an enrolled tax advocate in Dhaka can file your annual NBR return, attend hearings before the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes, and obtain certified tax clearance certificates on your behalf.
